accuracy.evidence: Checked against the named sources: working memory handles only a few new interacting elements while well-learned knowledge costs little (Sweller 1988; Sweller, van Merriënboer and Paas 2019; Cowan 2001 puts the limit at about 4 chunks); isolated-then-combined presentation helps with high element interactivity (Pollock, Chandler and Sweller 2002); small steps with practice after each (Rosenshine 2012); automaticity frees attention (LaBerge and Samuels 1974). Exchanging a ten for ten ones is the National Curriculum term for regrouping in column subtraction. The adult text says the 3 thinking slots and Try 5 scores are a picture, not a measurement, so no number is presented as data.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets five documented slips: more new things at once means faster learning (scene 1 prediction, challenge q1 and q4); right once but slow means ready (scene 3 prediction and the day-3 refusal, challenge q3); simplifying the goal instead of the surround (the Method dial refuses to turn known, challenge q2 and q6 'easy numbers are babyish'); jumping two steps (piano stairs refuse 'both hands, full speed' and the 3-change card); and staying easy for ever or giving up (challenge 'stuck' and 'avoid' feedback).

lab_distinct.evidence: The lab models this topic's own mechanism, counting what is new against a thinking-space meter and gating the next addition on fluency: tap new parts of Kai's page and watch 3 slots fill; turn 4 known/new dials with the goal locked new and run Try 5; drag a ready flag onto a 5-day log of score plus slow/easy for Kai then Zara; stack piano stairs where each must add exactly one new element. Lab-distinct gate passes (under 30% shingle overlap with every other flagship, including flagchunk, flagsteps and flagdelib), and none of those labs has a novelty count or a fluency gate.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers before the text confirms: finding the third new part turns the head red with 'Full: no room left to think'; Try 5 with 4 new things gives 1 of 5 and only reaches 5 of 5 once the learner has turned three dials back; the day-3 flag is refused as 'all right, but slow' before the day-4 flag lands; the stairs refuse any card that adds two things. Each step's done text (GOT) then states the rule the learner just met.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab then disproves: 'Yes: more new things, more learning' (the head overflows at 3); 'Yes: all right means ready' for day 3 (the flag is refused because it was slow); 'Both hands at full speed, to get used to it' (that card is refused on stair 1 with the named reason).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven questions rotate; every wrong option maps to a named slip in slip(): 'more' (more new things crowd the space), 'effort' (trying harder does not enlarge it), 'goal' (keep the thing you learn new), 'slow' (right but slow is not ready), 'stuck' (easy means ready for the next step), 'avoid' (cut it down, do not give up), 'babyish' (easy numbers leave room) and 'jump' (one stair adds one thing). Feedback is in a role=status live region with a Next one button.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use short sentences and concrete words (thinking space, swap a ten for ten ones, big numbers, right and easy) and pass the family kid limit in learn/validate_lessons.py; the adult text passes the adult limit. Canvas labels are short ('NEW: 4-digit numbers', 'Known: Plain sums', 'Day 4 5/5 all right easy') and every feedback line is one or two sentences naming the fix.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate is clean. Each kid paragraph adds one idea: a small thinking space; Kai's page with 3 new things; keep one new; ready means right and easy. Adult paragraphs give the research basis, the fluency link and what each lab scene does, the common mistakes with the caveat about the slot picture, and how the lesson differs from Chunking, Breaking tasks into steps and Deliberate practice.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 screenshots of every scene before and after Show me, plus a 1200 px desktop in dark theme: the head and 6 page tiles in 2 columns; 4 dial rows with two halves each and a Try 5 button with 5 result squares; 5 day columns with large scores; a pool of 5 piano cards over a 4-stair staircase whose labels sit on one or two lines; 8 sort cards in a 2 x 4 grid over two boxes. Real pointer drags at 390 px worked for a page tap, a dial tap, the flag to day 4, a card to stair 1 and a card to the One new thing box.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: 'New? …' per page part, 'Method/Numbers/Questions/Clock: make known/new' plus 'Try 5 sums', 'Flag day 1–5', 'Next stair: …' per card, and One new / Too much buttons per sort card, each with a full-sentence aria-label. The canvas aria-label carries the instructions and every result or refusal; challenge feedback is role=status; ticks, NEW labels and counts mark state as well as colour. The browser gate ran axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13 with no console errors.
